Description: Multi-domed sandstone structure built for the founder of the Lodi Dynasty. Citations: Sayyid Ahmad Khan (1847), 'Asar-us-Sanadid'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.

Octagonal tomb set in a walled garden, precursor to Mughal double-dome layout. Citations: Percy Brown (1942), 'Indian Architecture: Islamic Period'; Lucy Peck (2005), 'Delhi: A Thousand Years of Building'.

Large domed gateway attached to a richly decorated three-bay mosque in Lodi Gardens. Citations: Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'; Lucy Peck (2005), 'Delhi: A Thousand Years of Building'.
Signature Lodi mosque with sandstone and plaster filigree. Citations: Sayyid Ahmad Khan (1847), 'Asar-us-Sanadid'; Percy Brown (1942), 'Indian Architecture: Islamic Period'.
Elaborate three-storey stepwell with attached mosque and tomb in Mehrauli. Citations: Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'; Lucy Peck (2005), 'Delhi: A Thousand Years of Building'.
Cluster of prominent Lodi-era domed tombs in Green Park / Hauz Khas. Citations: Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'; Lucy Peck (2005), 'Delhi: A Thousand Years of Building'.
